solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: one thing sited in another is placed within it, so the word for unwell goes into the vessel

parts.note: an artery is a channel, for blood or for traffic
poorly means ill, unwell

explanation.surface: Badly positioned guns in the English Channel, a military blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' reads as an adverb on 'sited', but it is an adjective meaning unwell; 'sited in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is the collective term for large mounted guns of an army.

clue.text: A pain keeping dry for diplomat

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the pain word holds the dry abbreviation

parts.note: an ache is a pain
TT, teetotal, is the abbreviation for dry, not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A diplomat who is a pain and stays off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: TT (teetotal) means 'dry' in the sense of abstaining from alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a junior member of an embassy's diplomatic staff.

definitions.meaning: narrows or diminishes bit by bit, as a spire narrows toward its top
thin candles giving only a weak glow

explanation.surface: Someone slowly dimming weak lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means narrows off gradually; the noun names slender candles giving a faint light.

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone described as both sluggish and a little sulky.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the musical tempo marking meaning to be played slowly.

indicators.note: commonly signals dialect speech that drops the opening H, as in Cockney

parts.note: to catch a sound is to hear it

explanation.surface: Where you catch sound, put in a matter-of-fact way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks the dropped-H speech of Cockney London, turning HEAR into 'EAR; the definition 'in this' refers back to the whole: the organ sound is caught in.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing is the body part in which sounds are caught.

indicators.note: after places the scribble word following the betting word

parts.note: a Yankee is a bookmaker's bet combining four selections in eleven wagers
to doodle is to scribble idly

explanation.surface: Having placed a wager, someone jots down an anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: A Yankee is a British multiple bet on four horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee Doodle is an American song from the Revolutionary era, sung patriotically.

clue.text: Money taken from account: plot to return it

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the plot word is read backwards

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot, as in a flower bed

explanation.surface: A scheme to repay a sum withdrawn from a bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a scheme but is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A debit is an entry recording a sum withdrawn from an account.

clue.text: Dictated some moves, no longer wild

indicators.note: moves says these letters shift around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dictating a few chess moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' rearranges DICTATED SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamed animal has been brought under human control, so its savage state is past.

clue.text: Rail set in bar coming loose

indicators.note: coming loose suggests parts falling out of place and being reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A rail fixed into a bar is working itself free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming loose' rearranges SET IN BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister is the handrail at the side of a staircase.

clue.text: Hurry off after leaving gratuity? A simple game

definitions.meaning: read literally: put down a small reward for the waiter and dash away
an informal cricket game in which the batter must run whenever the ball is hit

explanation.surface: A diner tips and dashes out; also a basic game.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip-and-run is a casual form of cricket played in back gardens and on beaches.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated phrase names an easy-going cricket variant and literally describes tipping then running.

clue.text: Heavenly food in fashion, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: fashion means manner, way of doing, as in 'in this fashion'

explanation.surface: Divine cuisine is trendy, rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech MANNER and MANNA sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna is the food sent from the sky to the Israelites in the wilderness, in Exodus.

clue.text: Caution, about to handle inscribed tablet

indicators.note: about means going round, so the caution word goes round the handling word

parts.note: care is caution
to handle is to touch

explanation.surface: A warning about touching an engraved tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal here, not a vague 'concerning'; 'to handle' is a verb phrase supplying the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche is an oval tablet or frame bearing an inscription, as around pharaohs' names.

clue.text: Everyone taking a turn through small wood in fall

indicators.note: through places one piece passing within another

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

indicators.note: taking a turn means turning round, so the word for everyone runs backwards

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A group walking a lap through a copse in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' could suggest autumn in the surface; here it is the verb, to drop down.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to fall down suddenly.

definitions.meaning: one who tots up figures, a person adding numbers
to walk with faltering, wobbly steps

explanation.surface: A snake trying to move on wobbly feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adder' looks like the snake; it is someone who adds, i.e. tots up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tots figures up is one, and the verb means to stagger or wobble.

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
lots means many

explanation.surface: An unemotional girl turned down by many suitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses DILOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid describes a calm, unexcitable person who shows little emotion.

clue.text: Treatment of some music other people must accept

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the people word takes the music word inside

parts.note: they means other people, as in 'they say'
rap is a kind of music

explanation.surface: Music therapy that others are obliged to accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must accept' is the container signal: the people word takes the music inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is medical or psychological treatment for an illness or condition.

indicators.note: endless means with its last letter removed

parts.note: a barrier is an obstacle

explanation.surface: An unending hurdle for a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the final R from BARRIER.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie was the Scottish dramatist who wrote Peter Pan.

indicators.note: rearranged plainly asks for the letters to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: Brilliance shown in a court case that has been reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' reorders COURT CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To coruscate is to flash or glitter, and figuratively to be brilliantly witty.

definitions.meaning: begin working hard and in earnest
a brief bout of combat or quarrelling

explanation.surface: Getting serious and brawling.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means start work vigorously; as a noun it means a scrap or argument.

parts.note: to rap is to criticise sharply
ID, identification documents, means papers

explanation.surface: Quick to condemn the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' looks like newspapers; it is ID, identity papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means very quick, fast-moving.

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A turncoat executed at an eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like an execution; it reorders TRAITOR AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian eating house.

parts.note: as means so, in the sense of because
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A remark on how unusual a creature is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' looks like 'remarkable' but is S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a donkey, a hoofed beast of burden.

clue.text: Apparently good point by church in article

parts.note: pi, short for pious, describes someone sanctimonious, seemingly virtuous
E, east, is a compass point
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A seemingly good point beside a church, written in a report.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is slang for pious, smugly religious, hence 'Apparently good'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is an item or a written article, as in a newspaper.

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
very means absolutely, extremely

explanation.surface: A party that is truly a great find.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found for the first time.
